title: Recipe 26 — Template Marketplace (a signed registry, driven from the CLI)

beats.label: Open the recipe
beats.cue: “A registry is four methods and a trust root. The same interface covers a local directory, a git repo, an HTTPS index, or a Hugging Face mirror.”
beats.script: We’re opening the full walkthrough before changing anything, keeping the explanation and the implementation side by side. [[pause:1s]] A registry is four methods and a trust root. The same interface covers a local directory, a git repo, an HTTPS index, or a Hugging Face mirror.

beats.label: Start from a blank spec
beats.cue: live/ is scratch — the committed starter and the recipe are never touched by a take.
beats.script: We’re preparing a clean scratch state for “Start from a blank spec,” so this section starts from a repeatable baseline. [[pause:800ms]] live/ is scratch — the committed starter and the recipe are never touched by a take.

beats.label: Load the API key
beats.cue: [needs-key] Sources demos/.env into this one terminal.
beats.script: We’re loading the demo environment into this terminal session; credentials remain in the shell and are never written into the spec. [[pause:1.2s]] Sources demos/.env into this one terminal. Later credentialed beats reuse this exact shell environment without persisting the secret in the manifest.

groups.title: Beat 1 · the spec you would publish

beats.label: Type recipe 01's harness
beats.cue: “A template is a spec plus provenance. Start with the spec — the recipe-01 starter, unchanged.”
beats.script: The driver is copying the exact source-backed lines for “Type recipe 01's harness” into the scratch artifact now. [[pause:1.2s]] A template is a spec plus provenance. Start with the spec — the recipe-01 starter, unchanged.

beats.script: The terminal is running “Lint it” now; its output and exit status are the evidence for this beat. [[pause:1s]] Publish nothing that does not lint. A marketplace multiplies whatever you put in it.

beats.label: Show the lowered IR

beats.label: Compile the bundle — and check it
beats.cue: “--check asserts the shape, installs the deps, and boots it: GREEN with no key. That is the bar for anything you publish.”
beats.script: The terminal is running “Compile the bundle — and check it” now; its output and exit status are the evidence for this beat. [[pause:1s]] --check asserts the shape, installs the deps, and boots it: GREEN with no key. That is the bar for anything you publish.

verify.note: GREEN — assertion ok; install ok; boot gated at the provider credentials gate

beats.label: Open the emitted agent
beats.cue: “And this is what a consumer ends up with after install plus compile. No install-time code ran to produce it.”
beats.script: The editor is opening the generated agent for “Open the emitted agent,” so we can inspect the concrete artifact on screen. [[pause:1s]] And this is what a consumer ends up with after install plus compile. No install-time code ran to produce it.

beats.label: Make room for one manifest
beats.cue: “A LocalRegistrySource is a directory of name-dot-json files. One listing, one file — no per-template subdirectories.”
beats.script: We’re preparing a clean scratch state for “Make room for one manifest,” so this section starts from a repeatable baseline. [[pause:800ms]] A LocalRegistrySource is a directory of name-dot-json files. One listing, one file — no per-template subdirectories.

beats.cue: “Name, version, description, author, target, the spec YAML inline, the example env, and the publisher's key and signature.”
beats.script: The driver is copying the exact source-backed lines for “Type the recipe's manifest” into the scratch artifact now. [[pause:1.2s]] Name, version, description, author, target, the spec YAML inline, the example env, and the publisher's key and signature.

beats.label: List the catalog
beats.cue: “That is list — lightweight metadata for browsing, no spec bodies fetched.”
beats.script: The terminal is running “List the catalog” now; its output and exit status are the evidence for this beat. [[pause:1s]] That is list — lightweight metadata for browsing, no spec bodies fetched.

beats.label: Search it
beats.cue: “Search is name-priority: a hit in the name outranks a hit in the description. Author and target filter, they do not rank.”
beats.script: The terminal is running “Search it” now; its output and exit status are the evidence for this beat. [[pause:1s]] Search is name-priority: a hit in the name outranks a hit in the description. Author and target filter, they do not rank.

beats.label: Ask for a template outside the registry
beats.cue: “Exit 1 — invalid template name. A name that is not a plain identifier never reaches the filesystem, so submitting a template name cannot read etc-passwd.”
beats.script: This command intentionally exits 1; the nonzero status is the security or validation proof, not a failed demo. [[pause:1s]] Exit 1 — invalid template name. A name that is not a plain identifier never reaches the filesystem, so submitting a template name cannot read etc-passwd.

verify.note: deliberate rejection — exit 1: 'invalid template name "../../etc/passwd"' (the recipe's path-traversal refusal at every read)

beats.label: Install the template
beats.cue: “One file written: the manifest's yaml field, at workspace, name, crewhaus dot yaml. No env example, no post-install hook, nothing else.”
beats.script: The terminal is running “Install the template” now; its output and exit status are the evidence for this beat. [[pause:1s]] One file written: the manifest's yaml field, at workspace, name, crewhaus dot yaml. No env example, no post-install hook, nothing else.
beats.command: crewhaus templates use slack-bot --registry live/registry --into live/installed

beats.label: Open what landed
beats.cue: “Two lines and an ellipsis — because the recipe's manifest is an illustration, and its yaml field is elided. Install wrote exactly the bytes it was given.”
beats.script: The editor is opening the scratch CrewHaus spec for “Open what landed,” so we can inspect the concrete artifact on screen. [[pause:1s]] Two lines and an ellipsis — because the recipe's manifest is an illustration, and its yaml field is elided. Install wrote exactly the bytes it was given.

beats.label: Lint the installed spec
beats.cue: “Exit 1: agent required, channels required, routing required. Install does not validate — the compiler is the gate, and it does not care where a spec came from.”
beats.script: This command intentionally exits 1; the nonzero status is the security or validation proof, not a failed demo. [[pause:1s]] Exit 1: agent required, channels required, routing required. Install does not validate — the compiler is the gate, and it does not care where a spec came from.

verify.note: deliberate non-zero — exit 1: 'spec validation failed: agent: Required, channels: Required, routing: Required'. The recipe's manifest elides its yaml body, so what installs is the elided body; this beat shows the install path is real and unprivileged, not that the template is broken.

groups.title: One more thing · signing and publishing

beats.label: Run the registry smoke
beats.cue: “Here is the part no CLI flag exposes: verifyingRegistry refusing an unsigned manifest, an untrusted signer, and a tampered canonical JSON — plus TTL caching and the HTTP source.”
beats.script: The terminal is running “Run the registry smoke” now; its output and exit status are the evidence for this beat. [[pause:1s]] Here is the part no CLI flag exposes: verifyingRegistry refusing an unsigned manifest, an untrusted signer, and a tampered canonical JSON — plus TTL caching and the HTTP source.

verify.note: ALL PROBES PASSED — local source + traversal refusal, TTL cache + refresh, signature verification's three failure modes, HttpRegistrySource list/fetch

beats.label: Run the marketplace-client smoke
beats.cue: “And the client: list, name-priority search, install, then draftPublish — title, body, canonical manifest JSON, handed to your git client. The publisher never touches git auth.”
beats.script: The terminal is running “Run the marketplace-client smoke” now; its output and exit status are the evidence for this beat. [[pause:1s]] And the client: list, name-priority search, install, then draftPublish — title, body, canonical manifest JSON, handed to your git client. The publisher never touches git auth.

verify.note: ALL PROBES PASSED — constructor requires registry + workspaceDir, search ranking, install path, draftPublish manifestJson parseable, writeDraft persists
